reason: This passage (Ezekiel 37:1-14, the vision of the valley of dry bones) explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's goal to restore and help the Hebrew people (Israel). The text shows God opening their graves, raising them from death, returning them to the land of Israel (וְהֵבֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם אֶל־אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל), restoring their life through the spirit (וְנָתַתִּי רוּחִי בָכֶם וִחְיִיתֶם), and settling them on their land. The bones explicitly represent 'all the house of Israel' (כָּל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל). The entire passage is structured as a divine promise of restoration, revival, and renewal for the Hebrew people.
